purpose: This tool turns the idea of a limit into a game. You see what close means: someone picks a tolerance on the output, and you find how near to a you must stay to keep f(x) inside it.

stops.title: The graph and its bands
stops.text: The blue curve is f, and the yellow-ringed point sits at your chosen x. In the game modes a violet band is the allowed range of f(x), and a green band is the x values you choose. Red parts of the curve escape the violet band.
stops.try: Drag the ringed point, or any ring on a band edge. Each handle is an open ring at the edge.

stops.title: Three modes
stops.text: Approach shows a table of values closing in on a. Play with epsilon and delta shows both bands. Challenge gives you epsilon and you find a green band, using the Check my delta, No delta works and Next epsilon buttons that appear.
stops.try: Switch to Challenge, find a delta, then press Check my delta.

stops.title: Step closer
stops.text: Moves your x ten times nearer to a, and the table adds a row. Other side jumps to the other side of a. Reset sets x back to 0.1 away. These matter in Approach mode.
stops.try: Press Step closer four times. Watch f(x) settle.

stops.title: Epsilon, the output tolerance
stops.text: How far f(x) may be from the candidate limit L. A smaller epsilon is a stricter test, and the violet band gets narrower. You can also drag the violet edge on the graph.
stops.try: Make it very small and see how the curve escapes the band.

stops.title: Delta, the input distance
stops.text: How close to a you stay, shown as the green band. The point x = a itself is skipped. If the curve stays inside the violet band over the whole green band, your delta works.
stops.try: Shrink delta until the red parts disappear.

stops.title: Candidate limit L
stops.text: Your guess for the limit. Its height is the centre of the violet band. Drag the yellow dot or use this slider. A wrong L means no delta works, however small.
stops.try: On the jump function, move L to 1 and set Side to Left only.

stops.title: What Next does
stops.text: Step 1 approaches 2 for x squared. Step 2 shows the value at a does not matter. Step 3 plays the epsilon and delta game. Step 4 is a jump where no delta works.

teacher: Project step 3 and ask students to choose a delta for epsilon 0.1 before dragging. Ask: if delta works for epsilon, does a smaller delta also work? Misconception: that the limit is f(a). Step 2 shows a missing or changed value at a changes nothing.
